title: Accuracy of queried finite-family Fourier estimation
statement: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube, let $\\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of coordinate subsets, and let $0<\\varepsilon,\\delta\\le 1/2$. For each $S\\in\\mathcal F$, take the prescribed number of inputs and estimate its Fourier coefficient by the empirical average of $f(x)\\prod_{i\\in S}x_i$. If the Fourier weight of $f$ outside $\\mathcal F$ is at most $\\varepsilon/2$, and every estimated coefficient differs from its true coefficient by strictly less than $\\varepsilon/(2|\\mathcal F|)$, then the sign of the estimated Fourier sum has relative Hamming distance at most $\\varepsilon$ from $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
$\\mathcal F$ is a nonempty finite family of coordinate subsets
the Fourier weight outside $\\mathcal F$ is at most $\\varepsilon/2$
every empirical coefficient error is strictly less than $\\varepsilon/(2|\\mathcal F|)$
the sample inputs are indexed by each member of $\\mathcal F$ and by the prescribed sample count determined by $\\varepsilon,\\delta$
